text:
maya: FYI noticed spikes in TLS handshake failures for internal traffic to inference in us-east-1 and eu-central ~09:46 UTC. Error looks like session-ticket unwrap + cert verify path failing after yesterday's RBAC affine change.

jon: Samples?

maya: paste logs:
```
2026-06-06T09:46:12Z proxy[ingress-us]: TLS handshake error: session ticket unwrap failed: KMS Decrypt denied for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:... (principal=svc-cert-rotator)
2026-06-06T09:46:12Z proxy[ingress-eu]: certificate verification failed: signer chain incomplete after new cert rotated by cert-rotator
```

rachel: Checking audit stream, I see a dry-run RBAC rollout applied to the keystore role that removed broad `kms:Decrypt` in favor of a scoped binding. Dry-run should have been non-enforcing but appears to have been flipped.

infra_tool: Audit event: 2026-06-06T09:45:59Z IAM:UpdateRolePolicy role=keystore-agent-eu action=PutRolePolicy user=infra-deploy bot=policy-shipper mode=ENFORCING

maya: So cert-rotator uses the keystore role to unwrap session tickets and to access intermediate signing keys during rotation. If it can't Decrypt, it writes a partial chain and rotation completes but the proxy can't verify new chains. Ugh.

jon: Immediate mitigations?

rachel: 1) revert RBAC change to restore `kms:Decrypt` for keystore-agent in affected regions (us-east-1, eu-central) 2) issue a short-lived KMS Grant to the cert-rotator principal while we audit policy drift 3) mark the RBAC rollout as failed in the rollout dashboard.

ops-bot: runbook.trigger: emergency-grant -> creating KMS Grant for principal=svc-cert-rotator scope=Decrypt resource=alias/redwood-keystore-us duration=15m

cert-rotator: rotation log: new cert published at 09:45:36Z using key alias/redwood-keystore-us. Verification step returned partial chain, retry scheduled.

maya: After the emergency grant, handshake failures dropped in us-east-1 within 2 minutes. eu-central still degraded, looks like policy revert only applied to us-east earlier.

jon: Can we automate detection of RBAC-effecting changes that touch keystore roles? This is recurring.

rachel: Proposals: A) Add guardrail to policy-shipper: any PutRolePolicy touching keystore-* must run in shadow mode and require approval from security group. B) Add smoke-test in policy deploy pipeline that runs a keystore unwrap simulation in target region (uses staging ticket) and asserts KMS::Decrypt succeeds. C) Emit structured audit events from proxy when session unwrap fails that include KMS request id and principal.

maya: Also need short-term observability improvements: tag metrics when errors are KMS Deny vs crypto parse errors, and push KMS Deny counts to the RBAC dashboard.

infra_tool: Note: we currently only log `tls: session ticket` textually; will add structured JSON line: {"event":"session_unwrap_failure","region":"us-east-1","kms_request_id":"r-abc123","principal":"svc-cert-rotator","reason":"KMS:AccessDenied"}

jon: Post-incident action items: 1) Add keystore dependency smoke-tests to policy CI (owner=rachel) 2) Add preflight check in policy-shipper that refuses non-shadow keystore policy changes (owner=infra) 3) Make cert-rotator write to a verification bucket and fail rotations if chain incomplete (owner=maya) 4) Add an oncall runbook entry "RBAC change causing KMS denies".

rachel: I'll open a PR for the policy-shipper guardrails and add tests.

ops-bot: deployment:policy-shipper/revert-keystore-change v2026.06.06-hotfix -> started (id=deploy-8932)

maya: eu-central reverted ~09:59 UTC, errors dropped to baseline by 10:02. Confirming rotation health across regions.

jon: Long term: consider rotating session ticket encryption to a regional, short-lived key per region with an automated grant flow that is not present in general keystore policy, so RBAC changes are less likely to remove critical decrypt path. But that requires KMS quota and more infra changes.

rachel: Also recommend we add a binary test in infra-canary that actually completes a full rotation flow end-to-end every 4 hours in each region.

maya: Thanks. Filing INCIDENT-2026-1904 and assigning follow-ups. Will draft a short postmortem and include recommended changes to policy workflows and TLS hardening checklist. :eyes:
